claims.text: A compositionally graded refractory alloy interlayer can be used between W and CuCrZr.
The graded refractory alloy interlayer will improve bonding between W and CuCrZr.
The graded interlayer will mitigate thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The graded interlayer will limit chemical interdiffusion under fusion-reactor conditions.
Direct contact between W and CuCrZr inherently produces mechanical incompatibility because their material properties differ.
Direct contact between W and CuCrZr inherently produces thermal incompatibility because their material properties differ.
The proposed interlayer transitions from a tungsten-rich composition on the plasma-facing side to a CuCrZr-compatible composition on the heat-sink side.
Controlled spatial variation of alloy composition creates a gradual variation in interfacial properties.
A gradual variation in interfacial properties relieves stress accumulation at the W/CuCrZr interface.
A gradual variation in interfacial properties enhances bonding and resilience under reactor conditions.
The proposed interlayer will reduce thermal-stress accumulation relative to a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
The proposed interlayer will reduce residual-stress accumulation relative to a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
The proposed interlayer will decrease interdiffusion at the W/CuCrZr interface.
The proposed interlayer will enhance the durability of the bonded assembly under fusion-reactor operating conditions.
A direct W/CuCrZr interface suffers from high stress concentrations.
A direct W/CuCrZr interface suffers from chemical reactivity and degradation under extreme reactor conditions.
